sedonawineguide.caption:
Moms'-weekend crews who want one day where nobody has to plan or drive: this is the one. Our Sedona & Verde Valley Tour strings wine, craft beer, raw chocolate and lunch into a single private, all-inclusive afternoon, with your own guide behind the wheel.

Chocolate stop or lunch stop: which one is your crew's favorite? Tag the friend who'd skip straight to dessert.

#visitsedona #sedonawinetours

Sedona wine tasting where two waterways meet: Alcantara Vineyard sits where Oak Creek joins the Verde River, a rare riverside setting for Arizona wine. Our private Verde River Wine Tour with Alcantara pairs that tasting with a flexible day built around your group, with a guide and driver so nobody has to drive. Made for couples and small crews this October. Book your date below.

Girls'-trip crews with a beer fan or two in the mix: our private Verde Valley Brewery Tour turns the valley's craft taprooms into your afternoon. It runs 3 to 6 hours, fully private and built around your group, with hotel pickup and drop-off in Sedona or Flagstaff and water on board; several stops have food trucks or menus. Bride crews with one big dinner on the calendar: make the afternoon before it count. Our private Multi-Vineyard & Winery Tasting Experience puts your group in the Verde Valley vines with a guide and a driver, so the maid of honor can finally put the itinerary away. Couples driving up from Phoenix this weekend: October is when the Verde Valley starts to turn gold. On a private tasting day your own guide pours you through the region's tasting rooms while your driver handles every curve, so the only decision left is which vineyard patio gets your sunset. Proposal planners, Oak Creek has a mirror for you. At Crescent Moon Picnic Site, Cathedral Rock reflects in the creek, and through November the gate stays open until 6 p.m., so a late-afternoon visit lands right in golden hour. We love it as the finale of a private tasting day: Verde Valley vineyards after lunch with your own guide and driver, then the creek before sunset. Leashed dogs are welcome

Costume-squad friend groups, Halloween night in Sedona has a dance floor. Desert Disco - Halloween Bash runs Saturday, Oct 31, 6-10 PM at Outbound Sedona, with Pearl Charles live, DJ Alexander Sol and a costume contest.

Friend crews who'd rather make something than just buy a souvenir: on Thursday, Oct 29, Tlaquepaque's Calle Independencia hosts the Marigold Mural Project, a 26-foot community remembrance wall, from 11 AM to 5 PM with supplies provided. Birthday-weekend crews, here's your afternoon sorted: a willow-shaded pond, a few flights of Arizona wine, and nobody stuck driving. October is the tail end of harvest in the Verde Valley, so the tasting rooms have a buzz and the afternoons are made for sitting outside. We handle the van and the stops; you handle the toasts. Red or white first? Tag the friend who's planning the birthday.

Cornhole rivals and food-truck people, Saturday is yours. Fest of Fall takes over Posse Grounds Park on Oct 17 from noon to 6 with food trucks, a cornhole tournament, music and a Kid's Zone. Then give the other half of your weekend a slower pace: a small-group SIP tasting through Verde Valley tasting rooms, new friends at every stop and nobody stuck driving. Group-chat planners, here's the sunset move after a SIP tasting day: Airport Mesa. The overlook off Airport Road opens up a wide view of Sedona's red rocks, and in mid-October the sun drops right around 6 p.m. Spend the afternoon tasting Verde Valley wine with a small group (nobody has to drive), then head up the mesa while the rocks turn copper.

sedonawineadventures.caption:
Last-minute weekend planners with 90 minutes to spare: A Sedona Quickie was made for you. It's a 1.5-hour Sedona Wine Adventures stop at The Art of Wine in the Hyatt Piñon Pointe Shops, $95 per person, easy to fit between lunch and a sunset.

Think of it as your first taste of Verde Valley wine, then come back for a longer private tour later in the trip. Our tours are dog friendly, too. Quick stop

Dog parents, dust off the costume box: the Howl-o-Ween Costume Parade at Tlaquepaque is Sunday, Oct 18, 10 AM to noon, hosted by Tlaquepaque and BowWow Sedona to benefit the Humane Society of Sedona. It starts on Calle Independencia and finishes at Tlaquepaque North, with pet-themed vendors along the way ($20 entry). Ranch Winery Tasting takes your crew out of Sedona to a working family ranch turned boutique vineyard, with a guide, a driver and time to walk the vines before you taste. Bachelorettes with a few hours left before the drive home, this one's for you. A Sedona Quickie is our short-and-sweet private tasting, built for groups who are short on time but still want a real Verde Valley wine stop. It's private, so the pace is yours, and you pay the tasting rooms only for what you pour. Bringing the dog? We're dog friendly.
